\chapter{Fear, Anger, Sadness}
\label{ch:hi-fear-anger-sadness}
\hlchaptermodality{108}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say I am afraid, angry, sad or troubled, and tell someone not to worry.}

Complete HI-C108-chinta: name a feeling and answer someone else's.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[ḍar]{\hi{डर} (ḍar) — fear}

\label{lesson:HI-C108-dar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for weakness, then the Hindi for health.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{डर}}
\textbf{\hi{डर}} (\emph{ḍar}) — \textquotedblleft{}fear\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{मुझे} \hi{डर} \hi{लग} \hi{रहा} \hi{है}} — \textquotedblleft{}I am scared\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}fear is striking me\textquotedblright{}. Feelings take the \textbf{\hi{मुझे}} frame.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The first feeling.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mujhe ḍar lag rahā hai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for weakness, then the Hindi for health, then say \emph{ḍar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{डर} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Fear\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[gussā]{\hi{गुस्सा} (gussā) — anger}

\label{lesson:HI-C108-gussa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for health, then the Hindi for fear.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{गुस्सा}}
\textbf{\hi{गुस्सा}} (\emph{gussā}) — \textquotedblleft{}anger\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{मुझे} \hi{गुस्सा} \hi{आया}} — \textquotedblleft{}I got angry\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}anger came to me\textquotedblright{}, on the \textbf{\hi{आना}} you know.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A feeling that comes to you.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gussā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gussā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mujhe gussā āyā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for health, then the Hindi for fear, then say \emph{gussā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{गुस्सा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Anger\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[udās]{\hi{उदास} (udās) — sad}

\label{lesson:HI-C108-udas}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for fear, then the Hindi for anger.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{उदास}}
\textbf{\hi{उदास}} (\emph{udās}) — \textquotedblleft{}sad\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{मैं} \hi{उदास} \hi{हूँ}} — \textquotedblleft{}I am sad\textquotedblright{}. Like \textbf{\hi{बीमार}}, it describes you, so it takes \textbf{\hi{मैं} ... \hi{हूँ}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An honest answer on a bad day.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{udās}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{udās}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{maiṁ udās hūṁ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for fear, then the Hindi for anger, then say \emph{udās} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{उदास} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sad\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[pareśān]{\hi{परेशान} (pareśān) — troubled, bothered}

\label{lesson:HI-C108-pareshan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for anger, then the Hindi for sad.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{परेशान}}
\textbf{\hi{परेशान}} (\emph{pareśān}) — \textquotedblleft{}troubled, bothered, upset\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{आप} \hi{परेशान} \hi{क्यों} \hi{हैं}?} — \textquotedblleft{}why are you upset?\textquotedblright{}, with the \textbf{\hi{क्यों}} you know.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A question to ask a friend who looks upset.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pareśān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pareśān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{āp pareśān kyoṁ haiṁ?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for anger, then the Hindi for sad, then say \emph{pareśān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[cintā]{\hi{चिंता} (cintā) — worry}

\label{lesson:HI-C108-chinta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for sad, then the Hindi for troubled.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{चिंता}}
\textbf{\hi{चिंता}} (\emph{cintā}) — \textquotedblleft{}worry\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine.

\textbf{\hi{चिंता} \hi{मत} \hi{कीजिए}} — \textquotedblleft{}don't worry\textquotedblright{}, with the \textbf{\hi{मत}} that forbids.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Fear, anger, sadness, trouble, and a way to calm them.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cintā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cintā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{cintā mat kījie}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for sad, then the Hindi for troubled, then say \emph{cintā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{चिंता} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Worry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
